question: World Poverty Clock Report is released by which of the following?
solution:
The correct answer is __**World Data Lab**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **World Poverty Clock** is a tool developed by the **World Data Lab** to monitor progress against poverty reduction worldwide. 
• It was launched in **2017** and provides data on poverty in real time by estimating the number of people escaping poverty and those entering it. 
• The World Poverty Clock uses data from multiple credible sources, including **World Bank, UN, IMF, and national statistics agencies**. 
• Its key focus is on tracking progress towards achieving the **United Nations Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 1**, which aims to eradicate extreme poverty by **2030**. 
• The tool covers data from over **190 countries** and provides insights into poverty trends at both the global and regional levels. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **World Data Lab:** 
• **World Data Lab** is a social enterprise that specializes in building advanced data models and tools to measure global development challenges. 
• It provides forecasts and insights on key indicators such as **poverty, demographics, water security, and climate change**. 
• The organization is headquartered in **Vienna, Austria**, and collaborates with global institutions like the UN and World Bank. 
• The World Poverty Clock is one of its flagship projects, helping policymakers and researchers track poverty trends efficiently. 
• **World Bank:** 
• The **World Bank** is an international financial institution that provides loans and grants to countries for development projects. 
• It is focused on reducing poverty and promoting sustainable development worldwide. 
• The World Bank publishes key reports such as the **Global Economic Prospects** and **World Development Report** that include data on poverty. 
• While the World Bank is an important source of poverty data, it is not the creator of the World Poverty Clock. 
• **UNDP:** 
• The **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** is the UN's global development network, working to eradicate poverty and reduce inequalities worldwide. 
• UNDP monitors progress on the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** and assists countries in implementing policies to achieve these goals. 
• It provides poverty-related data but does not manage the World Poverty Clock. 
• **IMF:** 
• The **International Monetary Fund (IMF)** is an organization focused on global monetary cooperation, financial stability, and economic growth. 
• It publishes reports and provides data on macroeconomic indicators, including poverty levels. 
• The IMF contributes to global poverty data but is not directly involved with the World Poverty Clock. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Key Characteristics of the World Poverty Clock:** 
• It uses advanced data modeling techniques to estimate poverty levels in real-time. 
• The tool calculates the number of people escaping poverty per second and identifies regions lagging behind in poverty reduction. 
• It tracks poverty based on the **international poverty line** of living on less than **$1.90 per day**. 
• The World Poverty Clock is accessible online and is widely used by researchers, policymakers, and institutions. 
• **Connection to SDG 1:** 
• The World Poverty Clock aligns its data monitoring with **Sustainable Development Goal 1**, which focuses on eradicating poverty in all forms. 
• It provides actionable insights to help countries and organizations achieve the SDG targets by **2030**. </ul
